title: Multimodal RAG
blurb: Answers cited back to the page — including answers that live in a chart.

steps.say: This is multimodal retrieval augmented generation. Ordinary document question answering reads paragraphs. This one also reads the tables and the pictures.

You add a document here. A PDF is split three ways: the prose is chunked as text, every table is pulled out as structured rows, and every figure gets a caption written for it by a vision model. All three become searchable in the same index.

That third path is the point. A number that only exists inside a bar chart has no text anywhere in the file, so a normal search can never find it. Here the chart has been described in words, and the description is what gets matched.
You ask your question here, in any language, and it answers in the one you asked in.
Every answer is cited back to the page it came from, and clicking a citation shows you that page with the region highlighted, so you can check the answer against the source rather than trusting it.

It will also tell you when it cannot support a claim. A groundedness check runs over the answer, and a separate pass looks for statements in the documents that contradict each other. Add a document and try it, this one is live.
